title: Shell Programming
subtitle: Scripts, xtrace, and environment variables — flip to reveal meaning

cards.meaning: A file of the same commands you type; the shell interprets it line by line, finds each command, and runs it
cards.notes: Script = recipe the cook (shell) reads as it goes

cards.meaning: Shell reads script text at run time; a compiler turns a program into a machine-readable executable first
cards.notes: A binary can be called from a script; the script itself stays text

cards.front: why people like short shell scripts
cards.meaning: Syntax is simple; most short scripts work first time; debugging is straightforward (echo, run by hand, bash -x / set -x)
Prints each command to stderr just before it runs, after expansions; usual prefix is + (PS4)
cards.notes: Shows what the shell actually ran, not only what you typed

cards.meaning: Run the script with xtrace on for the whole process without editing the file
Turn xtrace on from that line (in a script or at a prompt)
cards.notes: Long name: set -o xtrace. Use when you only want a section

cards.meaning: Turn xtrace off
cards.notes: Minus = option on, plus = option off. Wrap only the block you care about

cards.meaning: Long name for set -x — same option
A name plus an associated value
Named value in the process environment; this shell and spawned children/subshells can read it
cards.notes: Memory: environment = inherited by kids. Become env via export

cards.meaning: Exists only in the current shell instance; a child does not inherit it unless exported
cards.example: Temporary counters, flags in one script
cards.notes: Memory: shell-only = stays in the room

cards.meaning: Assign a variable; no spaces around =
cards.notes: KEY = value makes the shell treat KEY as a command. NAME=value is one word

cards.meaning: Quotes if the value has spaces
Several values in one variable separated by : (how PATH works)
Names are case-sensitive — HOME and home are different
UPPER_CASE with _ between words (LOG_LEVEL, not logLevel)
Current logged-in user
Home directory of the current user
Default file editor (edit, visudo, crontab -e, tools that open an editor)
Path of the current user’s login shell (/bin/bash, /bin/zsh, …)
Name of the current user
Colon-separated list of directories searched when you run a command; first matching executable wins
cards.notes: A local ~/bin at the front can override /usr/bin

cards.meaning: Current locale settings
Current terminal emulation
Where the current user’s mail is stored
Print one variable (quote it)
Dump exported environment variables
Dump shell vars + environment + functions (lots of output)

cards.front: when not to use shell scripts
cards.meaning: Wrong tool for speed-critical work, complex/typed apps, mission-critical systems, security-sensitive algorithms, native multi-dim arrays, real data structures, graphics/GUIs, libraries/legacy code, or proprietary closed-source products
cards.notes: Glue and automation → shell. Product, performance, or secrets → another language
